title: What is RCS?
description: RCS is a messaging standard that lets you send text, images and files over the internet in your phone's messaging app. The name stands for Rich Communication Services. This means you do not need a separate RCS app.

title: How is RCS different from SMS and MMS?
description: SMS is text messaging over the mobile network. MMS can also contain images. RCS uses wifi or mobile data and can offer better media sharing, read receipts and interactive business messages.

title: What is RCS for business?
description: RCS for business lets a registered sender send messages with a company profile, images and selectable replies in the customer's messaging app. It is often called RCS Business Messaging, RBM.

title: What does a verified sender mean?
description: Verification checks the link between the RCS sender and the brand it represents. In Google Messages, the customer can see the company name, logo and a verification mark.

title: What are rich cards and carousels?
description: A rich card is a message card that can combine an image, a heading, a description and buttons. A carousel is several such cards that the customer swipes between, for example a selection of products.

title: How do RCS APIs and webhooks work?
description: An RCS API lets your systems request a message to be sent. Webhooks receive later events such as delivery, read status and customer replies. The API accepting the request does not yet mean the phone has received the message.

title: What does RCS on iPhone require?
description: RCS can be used in the iPhone Messages app from iOS 18, but the carrier and the plan must also support it. A system update alone is not enough.

title: How does RCS work on Android?
description: On Android, RCS is often used in Google Messages. When the app is connected, it can send over wifi or mobile data and show read receipts and typing indicators where supported.

title: How do I turn on RCS?
description: You turn on RCS in the messaging app's settings. The phone needs internet, correct number registration and support for the feature.

title: What does RCS cost?
description: Private RCS uses wifi or mobile data. The cost therefore follows your connection. Business messages have separate pricing from the service that sends them.

title: Is RCS secure?
description: It depends on which RCS service and which protection you mean. Verification helps identify the business sender. Encryption protects the content of the message. They solve different problems.

title: How did RCS develop?
description: RCS was developed within the mobile industry to give messages more features than SMS and MMS. The GSMA Universal Profile became a common technical foundation for apps, networks and services.

title: What is Universal Profile?
description: Universal Profile is the GSMA's common set of features and technical requirements for RCS. It is meant to make it easier for different apps, networks and services to communicate.

title: Does RCS need internet?
description: Yes, RCS needs internet over wifi or mobile data. A message to a recipient without a connection may have to wait or be sent through another channel.

title: What are the misunderstandings about RCS?
description: RCS is neither an app of its own nor a guarantee that all messages have the same features. It is a standard used by different apps and services.

title: What do the RCS terms mean in Swedish?
description: Agent means business sender, rich card is a message card and carousel is several cards you can swipe between. The words describe parts of RCS. None of them is an app of its own.

title: How is RCS used in marketing?
description: RCS can show an offer with a company name, image and buttons in the customer's messaging app. A card can present a product, and a carousel can give several options.

title: How can e-commerce businesses use RCS?
description: E-commerce businesses can use RCS for order confirmations, delivery status and product display. A delivery message can combine the order reference, current status and a tracking link.

title: How is RCS used in customer service?
description: With RCS, the customer can write to the company or choose a ready-made reply in the messaging app. Staff or a connected system must then take care of the question.

title: How do booking reminders work with RCS?
description: An RCS reminder can show the booked time and let the customer confirm or ask to reschedule. The choice is simple, but the booking system needs to handle the reply.

title: How are delivery notifications sent with RCS?
description: An RCS delivery notification can show the current status, a time window and a tracking link under the company's registered name. The customer should be able to see right away which order it is about.

title: How can restaurants use RCS?
description: A restaurant can send booking confirmations, show a menu with images or make an offer via RCS. A button can open the booking page or help the customer contact the restaurant.

title: Which rules apply to RCS campaigns?
description: The company is responsible for personal data and contact rules even when the campaign uses RCS. Phone numbers, replies and delivery data can be personal data if they can be linked to a person.

title: How do I measure the results of RCS?
description: ROI compares the value of a result with the cost of achieving it. RCS can provide delivery and read data, but a read receipt or a click is not a completed purchase.

title: How do I plan an RCS campaign?
description: An RCS campaign needs a goal, relevant recipients and a message that can be acted on. Choose the format by what the customer should do, and pay less attention to how many features exist.

title: What tone suits RCS?
description: A good tone in RCS sounds like a clear message from the company, without an advertising headline in every sentence. Say what has happened and what the customer can do.

title: What do Basic, Single and Conversation mean?
description: Basic, Single and Conversation are message types in business RCS, and they are not subscription plans. They describe different kinds of content and dialogue.

title: What are suggested replies?
description: Suggested replies are ready-made reply options that the customer can tap instead of typing. The Swedish name is föreslagna svar.

title: How do images and video work in RCS?
description: RCS can send images and video separately or as part of a rich card. How it looks depends on the file, the messaging app and the recipient's support.

title: How do I write a clear RCS message?
description: A clear RCS message first answers what the matter is about. Images and buttons should help the customer move on, and they are no reason to add more content.

title: What do action buttons do in RCS?
description: Action buttons in RCS can, for example, open a web page, call a number or show a location. They are called suggested actions and differ from ready-made replies that are sent to the company.

title: What is SMS fallback?
description: SMS fallback means that SMS is used as a backup when RCS cannot be sent or delivered according to the terms of the flow. It needs to be arranged in the service or the integration.

title: What does delivery status mean in RCS?
description: RCS status follows several steps in a send. Accepted means that the API has received the request. Delivered and read are later events when the service can report them.

title: What should be tested before an RCS campaign?
description: An RCS test needs to follow the customer's whole case: the message, the buttons, the reply and the update in the right system. A preview tests only one part.

title: What is a capability check?
description: A capability check examines whether a recipient can be reached by a business agent and which RCS features are supported. In Swedish it is called kapabilitetskontroll.

title: How is an RCS sender registered?
description: The company needs a registered and approved RCS sender before public campaigns. In Google's model, an agent is created, followed by brand verification and launch.

title: What is an Agent?
description: An agent is the company's sender on Google's RCS platform. It represents the brand in the messaging app and can be connected to the company's systems.

title: What is an Agent profile?
description: The agent profile is the company information shown for the RCS sender, such as the name and the logo. The customer should be able to recognize who is getting in touch.

title: What is an API?
description: An API lets one system request things from a service. In an RCS flow, the order system can use it to ask for a message when an order is shipped.

title: What is Asynchronous delivery?
description: Asynchronous delivery means that a message is handled after the first request. The system can get a response from the API before the customer has received the message.

title: What is brand verification?
description: Brand verification is Google's check of the link between an RCS agent and the brand it represents. An authorized representative confirms the details and the partner's right to manage the sender.

title: What is a suggested action?
description: A suggested action is a button that helps the customer do something, such as open a website. In RCS it is called a suggested action.

title: What is a carousel?
description: An RCS carousel is several message cards the customer can swipe between. It can show products or other options, with matching information on each card.

title: What is a delivery receipt?
description: A delivery receipt reports that a message has been delivered to the recipient's device, according to the service's status model. It arrives after the send has been requested.

title: What is a read receipt?
description: A read receipt is the messaging app's report of read status. It can help a company follow a send, but it does not show that the customer understood or accepted the message.

title: What is MaaP?
description: MaaP stands for Messaging as a Platform. It is a GSMA term for the platform support behind business communication over RCS.

title: What is MMS?
description: MMS stands for Multimedia Messaging Service and is a service for messages with, for example, images. MMS and RCS can appear in the same app but are different technologies.

title: What is an operator?
description: The mobile operator provides your subscription and can affect which RCS features you can use. This shows most clearly when an iPhone needs operator support.

title: What is P2P?
description: P2P means person to person. In RCS it refers to private chat, for example when two people write to each other in Google Messages.

title: What is postback data?
description: Postback data is information that comes along when the customer picks a reply or an action. The company's systems can use it to understand which choice was made.

title: What is RBM?
description: RBM stands for RCS Business Messaging, the business use of RCS. A company can send content under a registered sender and receive customer replies.
keywords: rcs business messaging rcs for business

title: What is RCS chat?
description: An RCS chat is a conversation that uses RCS over wifi or mobile data. Where it is supported, participants can share images, see read receipts and see when someone is typing.

title: What is an RCS client?
description: An RCS client is the app that handles RCS on the phone. Google Messages and Apple's Messages are examples of apps that can use the technology.

title: What is a rich card?
description: A rich card is a structured RCS card with room for media, a title, a description and choices. It can, for example, present a product with an image and a link.

title: What is a typing indicator?
description: A typing indicator shows that the other person is writing in an RCS chat. It says nothing about which reply is coming or whether anything is sent.

title: What is SMS?
description: SMS stands for Short Message Service and is the service for ordinary text messages over the mobile network. It does not need an active internet connection.

title: What is a webhook?
description: A webhook is an HTTPS address that receives events from a service. In RCS it can be a delivery status or a customer reply that needs to be passed on to your system.

title: Which Swedish operators support RCS?
description: Tele2 and Comviq state that RCS works on both iPhone and Android. For other Swedish operators, you need to ask about support for your subscription and your phone.

title: Does RCS work with Tele2?
description: Yes, according to Tele2's support. It states iOS 18 or later for iPhone and Android 5.0 or later with Google Messages for Android.

title: Does RCS work with Comviq?
description: Comviq says RCS works on iPhone and Android. Its support states iOS 18 or later for iPhone and Google Messages on a compatible Android phone.

title: How do I check RCS with Telia?
description: Ask Telia about RCS for your phone and your subscription. Apple's Swedish carrier list had no RCS marking for Telia on November 1, 2026, so it gives no confirmed yes.

title: How do I check RCS with Telenor?
description: Ask Telenor to confirm RCS for your subscription and say whether you use iPhone or Android. Apple's Swedish Telenor section had no RCS marking when checked on November 1, 2026.

title: How do I check RCS with Tre?
description: Tre needs to confirm whether RCS works on your subscription. When checked on November 1, 2026, Apple did not list RCS in its Swedish section for 3.

title: Can I assume RCS support from the carrier's network?
description: You cannot assume that Hallon, Fello, Vimla or Halebop have the same RCS support as the carrier whose network they use. Network coverage and messaging features are separate things.
keywords: rcs hallon fello vimla halebop network

title: Why do Apple's and the carrier's RCS statements differ?
description: Tele2 and Comviq confirmed iPhone support on their support pages on November 1, 2026. The same day, Apple's Swedish carrier list had no RCS markings. The pages gave different answers.

title: What happens to RCS when I switch carriers?
description: When you switch carriers, RCS may need to be checked again, even if you keep your number. The new carrier may have different conditions, especially for iPhone.

title: Why did RCS stop working after a SIM swap?
description: After a SIM or eSIM swap, the app's number registration or choice of line may need to be reviewed. First check that the right number is active and that the internet works.
keywords: rcs new sim esim not working

title: Which number does RCS use with dual SIM?
description: With dual SIM, RCS may use a different number than you intended. Check which line the conversation and the messaging app are set to.

title: Why is the RCS setting missing on iPhone?
description: The RCS option can be missing on iPhone when the carrier or subscription does not support the feature. Apple requires both a compatible iOS version and carrier support.

title: What do I do when RCS gets stuck on verifying?
description: When RCS stays on verifying, the number registration is not complete. First check that the app shows the right number and that the phone has internet.

title: Why does RCS only work with some contacts?
description: A phone can use RCS with one contact and SMS with another. Both participants must have working RCS in that specific conversation.
keywords: rcs only works with some contacts

title: How can I see whether a message is sent as RCS?
description: Read the channel text in the conversation's text field or the message details. The bubble color is not enough: on iPhone, RCS is green, just like SMS and MMS.

title: Does a green bubble mean it is SMS?
description: A green bubble on iPhone can be RCS, SMS or MMS. Blue bubbles are iMessage. Green therefore does not automatically mean SMS.

title: Does RCS work when I am abroad?
description: RCS can work abroad over wifi or mobile data. The app still needs to be connected, and both your subscription and the recipient must have support.

title: Does RCS work with a prepaid SIM?
description: RCS on a prepaid SIM needs to be confirmed by the carrier for that specific card. An answer about the carrier's subscriptions does not necessarily cover all prepaid cards.

title: What do I need to do with RCS when I change phones?
description: When you move your number to a new phone, check that RCS uses the right number there. The app should show that the connection works before you rely on it.

title: How do I turn off RCS?
description: On iPhone you turn off RCS under Settings, Apps, Messages and RCS Messaging. On Android the toggle is in Google Messages' settings for RCS chats.

title: Can I turn off business RCS on iPhone?
description: Apple describes a separate toggle for RCS business messages. It is under Settings, Apps, Messages and RCS Messaging when the feature is available.
keywords: turn off rcs business messages iphone

title: How do I block a business in Google Messages?
description: Open the business chat in Google Messages and use the app's options for blocking, reporting or unsubscribing. Which options you see can vary.

title: What happens in a group chat if someone lacks RCS?
description: A group where someone lacks RCS may get different features than an RCS group. What works depends on which channels the participants' apps can use together.

title: What should I include when I ask for help with RCS?
description: Support needs to know what is happening, when it started and which app you use. Add your phone model, system version, carrier and the RCS status you see.

title: How do you verify the sender of an RCS webhook?
description: An RCS webhook must check who is sending the request before it processes the event. Valid JSON or a known message ID does not prove that the request is genuine.

title: How do I handle duplicate RCS events?
description: The same webhook event may be received more than once without the customer's case changing several times. This is usually called idempotent handling.

title: What do I do if a webhook is delivered again?
description: If a webhook is delivered again, your system should be able to receive it without performing the same action a second time. Your provider's documentation sets the terms for redelivery.

title: Do RCS events have to arrive in the right order?
description: Plan for an event arriving later than it happened. The time your system receives an event does not have to match the time the message event occurred.

title: Why put RCS events in a queue?
description: A queue lets the webhook receive events quickly while the order or support system works at its own pace. It can be useful when processing takes time.

title: How do I link RCS to the right customer case?
description: Store which message ID belongs to which order, booking or support question. When replies and statuses come back, the system can then find the right case.

title: What should an RCS integration log?
description: A useful log shows the message identifier, timestamps and status from the request to later events. The full message text does not need to be copied into every log.

title: How do I protect API keys for RCS?
description: A secret API key should live in a protected server environment. Do not put it in the code of a web page, a public document or a support screenshot.

title: What happens if the RCS request is invalid?
description: An invalid RCS request can be rejected before any delivery begins. The error code shows whether the problem concerns, for example, format, permissions or content.

title: How should phone numbers be entered in RCS requests?
description: Follow the API's requirements for number format. International format with a country code is common, but your provider's documentation decides the details.
keywords: RCS phone number format country code

title: Why does an RCS message need a validity period?
description: A booking reminder that arrives after the visit helps nobody. A validity period sets a limit on how long a time-sensitive RCS message may keep trying to be delivered.

title: Can I stop a pending RCS message?
description: Some services can stop or revoke pending RCS messages. Whether it is possible depends on the service and on the message's status. Do not assume that a message that has already been delivered can be deleted on the customer's phone.

title: How do I avoid sending both RCS and SMS to the same customer?
description: A customer can receive both an SMS and an RCS message if a fallback SMS is sent while the RCS version is still waiting for delivery. Plan the two channels as one shared flow.
keywords: RCS SMS duplicate messages fallback timing

title: Can customers send files to a business via RCS?
description: Customers can send files in the incoming message types that Google's RCS for Business supports. Your service and your customer system also need to be able to receive and handle them.

title: How do I handle an unexpected customer reply in RCS?
description: Customers can type freely even when you have planned for reply buttons. The integration's reply handling therefore needs to cover more than the preset options.
keywords: RCS free text unexpected reply bot

title: How does a business handle a shared location in RCS?
description: Google's business model can receive a location from the customer. To use it, you need to link the location to the right conversation and know what it is going to be used for.

title: Do different brands need different RCS senders?
description: Several brands may need different RCS senders if customers recognize them as separate companies. Start from the identity the customer meets, and do not base it only on your internal organization.

title: What information is needed before an RCS launch?
description: Before a launch, the company needs to describe who the sender is, how the messages are used and how customers can reply or unsubscribe. Google describes such information in its launch material.

title: What is the difference between a test agent and a launched sender?
description: A test agent is used to try out content and integration with permitted test recipients. A launched sender has also passed the platform's approval for public sends.

title: How do I state response times in an RCS conversation?
description: Tell the customer when they can expect an answer from staff. An automatic acknowledgment shows that the question arrived, but it should not give the impression that the case is already resolved.

title: What does an RCS card need from a media URL?
description: The address of an RCS image or file must be retrievable the way the service requires. File type, size and access need to follow the provider's documentation.

title: Why is an RCS image cropped differently on different phones?
description: The image in an RCS card can be cropped differently depending on the card's layout and the phone. Do not place the most important detail of the product right at the edge.

title: What do I do when the recipient does not support an RCS feature?
description: If a recipient does not support a feature, you need to choose a simpler message or another channel. RCS support in itself does not confirm every carousel or action.

title: How do I detect that RCS events have stopped arriving?
description: Monitor both incoming RCS events and how they are processed. The API can accept a send even when delivery reports or customer replies do not reach your system.

title: How do I safely resume a stopped RCS flow?
description: After a stop, you first need to see which messages and events have already been processed. Resending the whole list can give customers duplicates.

title: How does RCS work for customers who use large text?
description: Test RCS cards and buttons with the phone's larger text settings. A preview with standard text does not show how it looks for customers who need larger letters.

title: How do I make RCS understandable with a screen reader?
description: An RCS message needs to be understandable through its text. If only an image states the time or the offer, a screen reader user can miss the message itself.

title: What should the first card in an RCS carousel show?
description: The first card needs to explain what the message is about. Some customers will not swipe further, so decisive information must not require a swipe.

title: How do I order products in an RCS carousel?
description: Place the products in an order that helps the customer choose. Show the same kind of details in the same place on every card so that comparison is easy.

title: How many buttons does an RCS message need?
description: The number of buttons should follow the customer's task. A tracking link can be enough for a delivery notice, while a booking may need both Confirm and Request rebooking.

title: When is free text better than reply buttons?
description: Reply buttons suit cases where the options are known. Free text is better when the customer needs to describe a problem, ask their own question or explain something unexpected.
keywords: rcs free text quick reply choice

title: What should the customer see after pressing a button?
description: After a button press, the customer should know what has actually happened. Request rebooking means that a request has been sent, and the new time is still to be booked.

title: How do I choose the language in an RCS send?
description: Choose the language based on what the customer prefers when you have that information. A Swedish phone number does not tell you which language the person wants to read.

title: Where should price and terms go in an RCS offer?
description: Show the price and decisive terms so that the customer understands the offer before the next step. Do not put an important limitation only in a small image caption.

title: Do emoji suit RCS messages from companies?
description: Emoji can suit business messages when they complement the text. They should not carry a time, a condition or the next step on their own.

title: How do I make sure an RCS link opens the right order?
description: An order link needs to be tied to the right purchase and the right access. The customer's phone number does not replace the authorization check on the page that opens.

title: Is an RCS preview enough?
description: A preview is enough to review a draft, but it is not enough to approve the whole send. The phone and the messaging app may display the content differently.

title: How do I write a link in a fallback SMS?
description: Write what the link opens and which case the fallback SMS concerns. Without the RCS card's buttons and images, the text needs to carry more of the context.
keywords: rcs fallback sms button link text

title: Can important information live only in an RCS image?
description: Do not put important information only in an RCS image. It can be cropped, load slowly or be hard to read on a small screen.

title: When is video useful in an RCS message?
description: Video works when motion explains something, for example how a product is used. A short status update rarely needs a film.

title: How do I use customer names without embarrassing mistakes?
description: Use a customer's name when the data is reliable. A greeting with the wrong name or a visible system field can make the rest of the message hard to trust.

title: How does the customer recognize the company in a long RCS conversation?
description: Keep the same recognizable business profile throughout the conversation and state which case each new message concerns. A name and a logo do not give the full context.

title: Does the whole purchase have to happen in the RCS chat?
description: The whole purchase does not have to happen in the RCS chat. A button can open a website where the customer pays, books or completes the order.

title: How does an RCS bot hand over to a human?
description: When automatic replies do not help, the customer needs to be able to reach staff. Confirm the handover and stop asking the same question if the customer has already answered.

title: How do I write a good error message in RCS?
description: A useful error message says what went wrong and how the customer can move forward. An internal error number needs an explanation.

title: How do I make recurring RCS messages less disruptive?
description: Send a new message when something relevant has changed for the customer. Every internal update does not have to become a notification.

title: Which time should a scheduled RCS send use?
description: Find out which time zone the scheduling uses. UTC and Swedish local time differ, and the difference changes with summer and winter time.
keywords: rcs schedule time zone daylight saving

title: How do I run a fair A/B test of RCS text?
description: A fair A/B test compares one limited change across equivalent groups. If you change the text, the offer and the send time at once, the cause of any difference stays unclear.

title: How do I keep several order messages together in RCS?
description: Write the order number or another relevant reference and what has changed. "Your order is ready" can be unclear to a customer with several orders in the same chat.

title: How do I keep the same message in RCS and SMS?
description: RCS and SMS need to say the same important thing, but with different design. RCS can have an image and buttons, while SMS needs text and a plain link.

title: What do I do when a customer objects to RCS advertising?
description: According to IMY, a customer has an absolute right to object to processing for direct marketing. After the objection, the personal data must no longer be used for that purpose.

title: Is an RCS reply consent to advertising?
description: A reply about a booking is not in itself consent to advertising. The customer may want to confirm a time without wanting to receive future offers.

title: How should RCS advertising be labeled?
description: Advertising in RCS must be recognizable as advertising, and the responsible sender must be clear. An offer should not be designed as if it were a necessary order message.

title: Can an order message also contain advertising?
description: Sending a necessary order message does not automatically give you the right to add advertising. Delivery information and a new offer have different purposes.

title: How do I stop advertising at all sending providers?
description: The opt-out has to reach every tool that controls the company's marketing sends. Otherwise the customer can be stopped in one service and remain in another.

title: Which customer details are needed in an RCS flow?
description: An RCS flow needs the customer details that are relevant to the case, and a copy of the whole customer profile is more than that. An order ID can be enough to find the rest in the customer system.

title: How long should RCS replies be stored?
description: No single retention period fits all RCS replies. How long they are needed depends on the case, the purpose and the requirements that apply to the business.

title: Who should be allowed to read customers' RCS replies?
description: Customers' RCS replies should be accessible to those who need them in their work. The fact that a system receives the replies does not mean that all employees should be able to read them.

title: What do I do if a customer sends sensitive information?
description: If a customer sends sensitive information, follow the business's procedures for that information. The fact that the data was sent voluntarily does not make further spreading or long storage appropriate.

title: Why do RCS statistics change after a send?
description: RCS statistics can change as new delivery and read events arrive. A report pulled right after a send is therefore not always the final picture.

title: How do I tell an RCS click from a purchase?
description: A click in RCS shows that the customer chose an action. A purchase is a later result that has to be confirmed where the order is completed.

title: Can I compare RCS reads with SMS deliveries?
description: RCS reads and SMS deliveries are different measures and should not be compared as if they meant the same thing. A delivery report does not say the customer has read the message.

title: What should customer service measure in RCS?
description: Customer service should measure whether the customer gets help, and whether the reply is read is only part of that. Time to a meaningful reply and the share of closed cases can be relevant metrics.
keywords: rcs customer service metrics response time

title: How do I calculate the cost when RCS has an SMS fallback?
description: Budget for RCS and the SMS fallback according to the service's own terms. A fallback SMS is not necessarily included in the price just because the send looks like one continuous flow.

title: Is a delivery report also an invoice report?
description: A delivery report shows the status of a message. An invoice report shows what was billed under the agreement. The two reports answer different questions.

title: Which customers should be part of an RCS pilot?
description: A pilot should include customers who fit the chosen use case and may be contacted. Internal test phones with the best possible support alone can give too narrow a basis.

title: When should an RCS pilot be paused?
description: Pause a pilot if customer data turns out wrong, unsubscribing fails or a reply is linked to the wrong case. An accepted API call does not make up for such errors.

title: What should I ask an RCS provider before buying?
description: Ask an RCS provider to show how your own flow works: which customers you can reach, how the sender is approved and how content, replies and the fallback channel are handled.

title: How do companies test reach to iPhone?
description: Test iPhone reach with the company's registered sender and the service you will use. A private RCS chat between two people does not test the same thing.

title: How do I interpret a news item about an RCS launch?
description: An RCS news item has to be read in its context: country, carrier, phone and type of use. Support for private Android chat is no statement about business sends to iPhone.

title: What should I check when the business profile changes?
description: A change to the company name or RCS profile may require a new review under the service's rules. You cannot assume an approved sender is free to change brand.

title: Should support and marketing use the same RCS sender?
description: Support and marketing may need the same recognizable RCS identity when they represent the same brand. The organization's internal boundaries do not have to be visible to the customer.

title: What should be checked before a customer list is used for RCS?
description: Check phone numbers, duplicates and current opt-outs before a customer list is used. The recipients also need to be allowed to be contacted for the purpose of the send.

title: How may customer results be described in RCS marketing?
description: Customer results need to be verifiable. Describe what was measured and in which campaign, and avoid turning a single figure into a promise for all customers.

title: How do I keep information about RCS support up to date?
description: Information about RCS support needs a date for the check and a clear source. An old launch news item is not always enough for a current answer.

title: How do I test RCS between two carriers?
description: Test with two phones that have working RCS and different carriers. Check the connection status on both before you start.
